featureName: MCP task in the real app
headline: Connect an agent, create a task, watch it land
overview: This walkthrough crosses the boundary the protocol-only demo cannot: DoneOS explains the connection in its own settings, accepts a real MCP write, shows the resulting task in Queue, and attributes the event to the connected agent in Activity.
targetAudience: People deciding whether MCP changes the product or only the developer console

steps.title: Connection starts inside DoneOS
steps.action: Opened Connect and inspected the AI Agents panel.
steps.description: DoneOS explains what the MCP credential does before it asks for one: the connected agent can work the shared Queue, and every action is attributed in Activity. The empty state shows the supported clients and makes it clear that a key does not start an agent by itself.
steps.screenshotAlt: DoneOS Connect screen showing AI agent setup and its attribution model

steps.title: The connected credential reports its use
steps.action: Connected with the generated local credential, then created and independently read back a task through the official MCP SDK.
steps.description: After the call, the credential appears as Walkthrough Agent with its usage state inside the product. The one-time token never appears in the capture.
steps.screenshotAlt: DoneOS Connect screen showing the Walkthrough Agent credential after an MCP call

steps.title: The MCP task is now real app work
steps.action: Opened Execute, then Queue after the MCP write completed.
steps.description: The exact high-priority task created through MCP appears in DoneOS beside the normal app controls. It is not a terminal transcript or a mocked result; this is the Flutter product reading the same emulator-backed state.
steps.screenshotAlt: DoneOS Queue showing the exact task created through MCP

steps.title: Activity keeps the agent accountable
steps.action: Opened Activity and found the creation event.
steps.description: DoneOS records the write as an execution event attributed to Walkthrough Agent. That closes the user-facing loop from connection settings, to MCP action, to visible task, to an auditable history.
steps.screenshotAlt: DoneOS Activity showing the MCP-created task attributed to Walkthrough Agent

keyFeatures: Official MCP SDK write and independent read-back
The exact task visible in the Flutter Queue
tips: All account and task data in this walkthrough is fictional and exists only in local emulators.
note: Live-walked against the committed DoneOS Flutter app and local Firebase emulators. The disposable credential was never shown and disappears when the emulator session ends.
